title: Dubai Off-Plan Sales Fell 38%. But Buyers Did Not Disappear
seoTitle: Dubai Off-Plan Sales Fell 38%, but Buyers Did Not Disappear
description: Dubai home sales dropped 38% in Q3 2026, yet 72% of sales were still off-plan. Why the buyer did not leave the market, and what careful buyers want.
answer: As of October 2026, Dubai recorded about 34,000 home sales in the third quarter, 38% fewer than a year earlier. Yet about 72% of those sales were off-plan. Buyers did not leave the market. They became careful. They now ask whether a project is real, whether it will be delivered, and exactly what they are buying.
body:
A 38% drop in sales sounds like buyers ran away. Look one number deeper and the picture changes.

## What the Q3 2026 numbers show

As reported for the third quarter of 2026, Dubai recorded about 34,000 home sales. That is 38% fewer than the same quarter a year earlier. The value of those sales fell even more, about 47%, to around 72 billion dirhams. In September alone, sales were down more than 40% compared with the previous September.

This came after four years in which Dubai was not running, it was sprinting. Then the war that started at the end of February stopped it suddenly. A sprinter who is stopped does not just slow down. They have to catch their breath.

## The number that matters most: 72%

Even in this market, almost three out of four homes sold in Dubai were off-plan, about 72%. People still choose to buy off-plan rather than existing homes. The demand for new projects is still there. What changed is how buyers decide.

## Careful, not absent

When a market is sprinting, buyers buy almost anything on offer. When it catches its breath, they start asking questions:

- Is this project real?
- Will it be delivered?
- What exactly am I buying?

These are not the questions of someone leaving. They are the questions of someone who still wants to buy, but wants to be sure first.

## What this means for developers

The year of selling on hype is over, at least for now. The developers who answer those three questions clearly will keep selling. The others will have to compete on discounts. In my view, certainty is the biggest opportunity in this market.

This short comes from a full episode with the price data, the supply outlook and my forecast. Listen at [/podcast/dubai-off-plan-correction-or-crash-my-forecast/](/podcast/dubai-off-plan-correction-or-crash-my-forecast/).
takeaways: Dubai home sales fell 38% year over year in Q3 2026, to about 34,000.
About 72% of homes sold were still off-plan.
Buyers did not disappear; they became careful.
Careful buyers ask whether a project is real, whether it will be delivered, and what they are buying.
Developers who answer those questions clearly keep selling without heavy discounts.
